editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing would mislead a learner: the optimality claim, the no-extra-circuits caveat and the noise-drift caveat in [20] are all intact. 'Expectation value' is rendered everywhere as 'expected value', which is a different English term from the physics one this page uses. 'Measurement' is often rendered as bare 'sukat', which reads as 'size/measure' rather than the act of measuring, so 'karagdagang sukat' in [13] and [15] is ambiguous. In [11], 'mitigating' becomes 'inaaayos' (which is also a typo for 'inaayos', 'fixing'), overstating mitigation as correction, and 'paganahin ang quantum advantage' in [13] is a calque.

examples.source: mitigating the inevitable noise-induced errors
examples.translation: habang inaaayos ang mga hindi maiiwasang error na dulot ng ingay
examples.suggested: habang binabawasan ang mga hindi maiiwasang error na dulot ng ingay
examples.why: 'Inaayos' (misspelled here as 'inaaayos') means fixing or correcting. That overstates error mitigation, which reduces errors; it does not remove them.

examples.source: informationally complete measurements ... number of additional measurements
examples.translation: informationally complete na sukat ... bilang ng karagdagang sukat
examples.suggested: informationally complete na pagsukat ... bilang ng karagdagang pagsukat
examples.why: 'Sukat' means a size or quantity. 'Pagsukat' is the act of measuring, which is what the source means. The same issue appears in [15] and [17].

examples.source: error-mitigated expectation values
examples.translation: mga error-mitigated expected value
examples.suggested: mga error-mitigated expectation value
examples.why: The English is 'expectation value', the standard quantum term. The whole file uses 'expected value' instead ([11], [13], [24], [27]).

examples.source: TEM has the potential to enable quantum advantage
examples.translation: ang TEM ay may potensyal na paganahin ang quantum advantage
examples.suggested: maaaring maging daan ang TEM tungo sa quantum advantage
examples.why: 'Paganahin' means to make a device run, so here it is a literal calque of 'enable' and reads stiffly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The caveat in [3] ("maaaring gumamit ang instance ng higit sa nakalaan nitong oras"), the list of what happens at the limit in [8]-[11], and the Flex vs. Premium condition in [12] all match the source, and the register stays casual with no po/opo. The one slip is in the heading at [13]. It renders "different values" as "iba't ibang halaga", which reads as "various values". The point is two values that differ from each other, so "magkaibang halaga" is the idiomatic choice.

examples.source: Set different values for the allocation limit and usage limit
examples.translation: Magtakda ng iba't ibang halaga para sa allocation limit at usage limit
examples.suggested: Magtakda ng magkaibang halaga para sa allocation limit at usage limit
examples.why: "iba't ibang" means 'various/assorted'. The heading contrasts two values that differ from each other, which Tagalog expresses with "magkaiba".

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall, and nothing in it would mislead a learner. The cost, queueing and Open Plan caveats all come through, and the PEA/PEC noise-model explanation in [39] is accurate. A few spots should still be fixed. In [15] and [45], "as tightly/closely together as possible" becomes "nang magkakasabay" ("simultaneously") and the "as possible" is dropped. That sits awkwardly next to [29], which says a QPU runs only one job at a time. In [8], "significantly faster" loses "significantly". In [35], "Evaluate the cost function" is rendered as "Suriin" ("examine") instead of a word for computing it. In [39], "learn the noise model" is calqued as "matuto ng noise model", which reads as a person learning.

examples.source: it's beneficial that they run as closely together as possible
examples.translation: makakatulong na mapatakbo ang mga ito nang magkakasabay
examples.suggested: makakatulong na mapatakbo ang mga ito nang magkakalapit hangga't maaari
examples.why: 'magkakasabay' means simultaneous, which conflicts with the one-job-at-a-time QPU in [29]. The source means close together in time, and 'as possible' was dropped.

examples.source: experiments that need to run as tightly together as possible
examples.translation: mga eksperimento na kailangang mapatakbo nang magkakasabay
examples.suggested: mga eksperimento na kailangang mapatakbo nang pinakamalapit hangga't maaari sa isa't isa
examples.why: Same shift from 'close in time' to 'simultaneous', which gives the wrong picture of how a session runs jobs.

examples.source: running multiple jobs in a batch is significantly faster than running them serially
examples.translation: mas mabilis kaysa sa paisa-isa
examples.suggested: lubhang mas mabilis kaysa sa paisa-isa
examples.why: The intensifier 'significantly' is dropped, which weakens the claim.

examples.source: Evaluate the cost function on a QPU.
examples.translation: Suriin ang cost function sa isang QPU.
examples.suggested: Kalkulahin ang cost function sa isang QPU.
examples.why: 'Suriin' means inspect or analyze. Evaluating a cost function means computing its value.

examples.source: you can learn the noise model once
examples.translation: maaari kang matuto ng noise model nang isang beses
examples.suggested: maaari mong i-learn (tukuyin) ang noise model nang isang beses
examples.why: 'matuto' is a person learning something, not a system characterizing noise. It is a calque and reads oddly here.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The role requirements in [5] (Administrator for rules, Editor or Administrator for network zones, Viewer can "makakapagdagdag lamang") match the English, and so do the caveats in [4] and [6]. The one thing a native editor would fix is the compromised-credentials phrase in [4], "may mga nakompromisong o maling pinamamahalaang kredensyal". It puts a linker on the first adjective before "o" and uses the progressive "pinamamahalaan", so it reads stiff and ungrammatical. Keeping "resources" and "context-based restrictions" in English is a reasonable choice and is used the same way everywhere.

examples.line_approx: Dahil parehong nagpapatupad ng access ... kahit na may mga nakompromisong o maling pinamamahalaang kredensyal.
examples.source: context-based restrictions offer protection even in the face of compromised or mismanaged credentials.
examples.translation: ang context-based restrictions ay nagbibigay ng proteksyon kahit na may mga nakompromisong o maling pinamamahalaang kredensyal.
examples.suggested: ang context-based restrictions ay nagbibigay ng proteksyon kahit na nakompromiso o hindi maayos na napamahalaan ang mga kredensyal.
examples.why: The linker on 'nakompromisong' before 'o' is ungrammatical. The progressive 'pinamamahalaang' means 'being managed' and doesn't fit a past mismanagement, so the phrase reads as a word-by-word calque.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The AQC-Tensor workflow in [7] and [23], the dry-run caveat in [28] and the logging guidance in [17] and [42] all match the English. "Remotely" is translated two ways: "nang remote" in [14], but the literal "nang malayo" (meaning physically far away) in [33], [38] and [39]. There are also two typos, "nagbababalik" in [19] and "nabuong sa proseso" in [31], plus some stiff phrasing: "Pagkatapos na tumatakbo na ang job" in [42] and "ngunit na may" in [23].

examples.source: The previous section created a program to be run remotely.
examples.translation: Ginawa ng nakaraang seksyon ang isang program na tatakbo nang malayo.
examples.suggested: Gumawa ang nakaraang seksyon ng program na patatakbuhin nang remote.
examples.why: 'nang malayo' is a literal calque meaning physically far. It also clashes with 'nang remote' in [14]. The same issue appears in [38] and [39].

examples.source: returning an informative error message
examples.translation: nagbababalik ng impormatibong mensahe ng error
examples.suggested: nagbabalik ng malinaw na mensahe ng error
examples.why: Typo: the syllable is doubled in 'nagbababalik'. 'impormatibong' is also a stiff calque.

examples.source: important metadata generated along the way
examples.translation: mahahalagang metadata na nabuong sa proseso
examples.suggested: mahahalagang metadata na nabuo sa proseso
examples.why: Grammar slip: 'nabuong' carries a stray linker.

examples.source: After the job is running, you can fetch logs
examples.translation: Pagkatapos na tumatakbo na ang job, maaari kang kumuha ng mga log
examples.suggested: Kapag tumatakbo na ang job, maaari mo nang kunin ang mga log
examples.why: 'Pagkatapos na tumatakbo na' is an awkward calque of the English. A native writer would use 'Kapag ... na'.

examples.source: an ansatz is generated from an equivalent circuit but with fewer Trotter steps
examples.translation: mula sa isang katumbas na circuit ngunit na may mas kaunting mga Trotter step
examples.suggested: mula sa katumbas na circuit pero may mas kaunting Trotter step
examples.why: 'ngunit na may' is ungrammatical because of the stray 'na'. It reads as machine translation.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The numbers, the ordering of trajectories from lowest to highest cost, the population_size rule of thumb and the benchmark comparisons all match the English, so nothing would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix a few small slips. In [37], "sharply concentrated" became "mabilis na nakakonsentra" ("quickly concentrated"), and "update the count column accordingly by" came out garbled as "ayon sa pamamagitan ng". In [21], "non-trading days" became "araw na hindi nagtatrabaho" ("non-working days"). There are also grammar slips: "para malutas ng QUBO" in [10] and "maaari kang ma-access" in [33]. Smaller points: [36] mixes in English ("hayagang at consistently"), [28] drops "much" from "much faster", and [11] drops "post" from "post-processed".

examples.source: is sharply concentrated at lower objective cost values
examples.translation: ay mabilis na nakakonsentra sa mas mababang mga halaga ng objective cost
examples.suggested: ay matinding nakakonsentra sa mas mababang mga halaga ng objective cost
examples.why: 'mabilis' means fast/quickly. That reads as a time property, but the English describes the shape of the distribution (narrow and peaked).

examples.source: Then, update the count column accordingly by joining counts of identical rounded values.
examples.translation: Pagkatapos, i-update ang column ng bilang ayon sa pamamagitan ng pagsasama ng mga bilang...
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos, i-update ang column ng bilang sa pamamagitan ng pagsasama ng mga bilang...
examples.why: 'ayon sa pamamagitan ng' is ungrammatical: 'accordingly' was calqued as 'ayon sa' and stacked onto 'sa pamamagitan ng'.

examples.source: we have filled non-trading days with the closing price
examples.translation: pinuno namin ang mga araw na hindi nagtatrabaho ng closing price
examples.suggested: pinuno namin ang mga araw na walang kalakalan ng closing price
examples.why: 'hindi nagtatrabaho' means non-working days, not days when the markets are closed for trading.

examples.source: you can access the results of all the sampled strategies
examples.translation: maaari kang ma-access ang mga resulta
examples.suggested: maaari mong i-access ang mga resulta
examples.why: Grammar slip: 'ma-access' with 'kang' is the wrong verb form here.

examples.source: to solve a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem
examples.translation: para malutas ng Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) na problema
examples.suggested: para malutas ang Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) na problema
examples.why: The marker is wrong: 'ng' should be 'ang' because the QUBO problem is the thing being solved.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally in a casual register. It keeps the cloud terms the field leaves in English (high availability, disaster recovery, load balancer, single point of failure), and "Walang kapansin-pansing pagbaba ng kalidad ng serbisyo" in [9] carries the no-degradation claim correctly.

The meaning is faithful all through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. Instructions like "Patakbuhin ang command na ito para i-install..." and the pip upgrade advice match the English exactly, and the casual register holds. Two entries add parenthetical English glosses that aren't in the source: "requirements (dependency spec)" in [9] and "source (source code)" in [11]. They're redundant and read like translator notes, so a native editor would remove them.

examples.source: We recommend frequently updating your requirements for `qiskit-ibm-runtime`
examples.translation: Inirerekumenda naming madalas na i-update ang iyong requirements (dependency spec) para sa `qiskit-ibm-runtime`
examples.suggested: Inirerekumenda naming madalas na i-update ang iyong requirements para sa `qiskit-ibm-runtime`
examples.why: The English gloss '(dependency spec)' isn't in the source. It's a translator note that makes the sentence clunkier and adds nothing for the reader.

examples.source: Install the Qiskit SDK from source
examples.translation: I-install ang Qiskit SDK mula sa source (source code)
examples.suggested: I-install ang Qiskit SDK mula sa source code
examples.why: The parenthetical just repeats the same English word. Use 'source code' once instead of glossing it.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally in a casual register. It keeps the caveat "(maaaring magkaroon ng bayad)" for App ID, renders users consistently as "mga gumagamit", and correctly says in the tip that dynamic rules mean "hindi mo na kailangang manu-manong idagdag" each user.

The meaning is faithful throughout. The shots/cost scaling, the Estimator precision caveat, the error-suppression warning and the NoiseLearner staleness caveat ("praktikal lang ito kung...", "sa loob ng isang session") all carry over correctly. The only thing a native editor would change is in entry [7]: "walang mahabang pagitan sa pagitan ng mga job" repeats "pagitan" and reads stiffly. The casual register holds with no po/opo, and job/shots/Estimator are consistently kept in English.

examples.source: so this is only practical if there is no long delay between jobs
examples.translation: kaya praktikal lang ito kung walang mahabang pagitan sa pagitan ng mga job
examples.suggested: kaya praktikal lang ito kung hindi matagal ang pagitan ng mga job
examples.why: 'pagitan sa pagitan' repeats the same word and reads like a calque of 'delay between'. Rephrasing it avoids the repetition.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The events table (entry 10) keeps every action and API endpoint accurate, and the audit and compliance purpose in entry 4 is intact. I found two naturalness slips a native editor would fix. In entry 5, "mga destinasyon ng iyong pagpili" is a word-for-word calque of "destinations of your choice", and "mga destinasyong pipiliin mo" reads more naturally. In entry 3, "nagbubuo" is not the idiomatic verb form for "generate", and "bumubuo" is the usual choice.

examples.source: to route auditing events in your account to destinations of your choice
examples.translation: patungo sa mga destinasyon ng iyong pagpili
examples.suggested: patungo sa mga destinasyong pipiliin mo
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of the English "of your choice". Tagalog normally puts this in a relative clause.

examples.source: IBM Cloud services ... generate activity tracking events.
examples.translation: ay nagbubuo ng mga kaganapan sa pagsubaybay ng aktibidad
examples.suggested: ay bumubuo ng mga kaganapan sa pagsubaybay ng aktibidad
examples.why: "Nagbubuo" is a nonstandard verb form here. "Bumubuo" is the idiomatic way to say "generate".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The deprecation timeline (early 2025, deprecated in SDK v1.3.0, removed in v2.0.0), the Heron-only `use_fractional_gates` flag and the Qiskit Dynamics pointers all match the English. Terminology is consistent: fractional gates, pulse-level na kontrol, i-calibrate and transpilation pipeline all stay the same across the file. One slip: entry [5] describes the old, now-deprecated workflow without any past-tense marker, and ends with the present-tense 'lumilikha ito ng calibration'. That reads as if this is still how things work, so a native editor would add 'dati' and switch the verb to 'lumikha'.

examples.source: The most common use-case of pulse-level control was ... In the background this created a *calibration*
examples.translation: Ang pinakakaraniwang gamit ng pulse-level na kontrol ay ... Sa background, lumilikha ito ng *calibration*
examples.suggested: Ang pinakakaraniwang gamit dati ng pulse-level na kontrol ay ... Sa background, lumikha ito ng *calibration*
examples.why: The English uses the past tense ('was', 'created') to describe a workflow that has been deprecated. The Tagalog has no past-tense marker and uses the present-tense 'lumilikha', which slightly blurs that this is the old approach.

editor_note: Faithful, casual Taglish that keeps the key caveat that Qiskit 1.0 "hindi ito compatible sa lahat ng nakaraang bersyon", and uses "Gabay sa migration" and "breaking package changes" the same way on all three linked guide titles.

Faithful and natural in the casual register, keeping the field's English terms consistent ("template implementation", "base template", "Hamiltonian simulation") and rendering "best practices" as "pinakamahusay na gawi" in both [6] and [13].

The translation is accurate and reads naturally. "Encrypted at rest" becomes "ine-encrypt habang nakaimbak", the three-year retention while you are a current user (undeleted data only) is kept exactly in [10], and the Manager-role condition for deleting individual jobs in [8] is preserved.

Faithful and natural throughout: the one substantive paragraph [3] keeps the strength of the English ("vitally important" becomes "Napakahalaga", "strongly recommended" becomes "lubos na inirerekumenda"), renders "out-of-date dependencies" as "mga lumang dependency", and uses "mga patakaran sa seguridad" consistently.

The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing on the page would mislead a learner. There are a few naturalness slips. In [18], "ay sino-subject sa benchmarking" is an awkward English calque. In [20], "performant foundation" is weakened to "matibay na pundasyon" ("sturdy foundation"), which drops the speed/performance nuance. In [26], "naglulutas para sa" copies English "solves for", and in [24], "na may o walang noise" copies English word order.

examples.source: the Qiskit SDK is benchmarked using over 1,000 tests
examples.translation: ang Qiskit SDK ay sino-subject sa benchmarking gamit ang mahigit 1,000 na test
examples.suggested: bina-benchmark ang Qiskit SDK gamit ang mahigit 1,000 test
examples.why: 'sino-subject sa' is a stiff hybrid calque. The plain Taglish verb 'bina-benchmark' is what a native writer would use.

examples.source: build upon Qiskit's performant foundation of tools
examples.translation: nagtatayo sa matibay na pundasyon ng Qiskit ng mga kasangkapan
examples.suggested: nakabatay sa mabilis at mahusay na pundasyon ng mga kasangkapan ng Qiskit
examples.why: 'performant' is about speed and efficiency, but 'matibay' means sturdy. This is a small shift in emphasis, not a misleading one. 'nagtatayo sa' is also a literal calque of 'build upon'.

examples.source: solves for corrected measurement probabilities
examples.translation: naglulutas para sa mga corrected measurement probability
examples.suggested: kumakalkula ng mga naitamang measurement probability
examples.why: 'naglulutas para sa' copies the English 'solves for' word for word. It is unidiomatic in Tagalog.

examples.source: run quantum circuits with or without noise
examples.translation: magpatakbo ng mga quantum circuit na may o walang noise
examples.suggested: magpatakbo ng mga quantum circuit, may noise man o wala
examples.why: 'na may o walang' keeps the English structure and reads stiffly. The 'may ... man o wala' construction is more natural.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The per-plan definitions of Instance usage all match the English: rolling 28 days for Premium and Open, everything since the instance was created for Pay-As-You-Go, and everything since the contract began for Flex. The register stays casual throughout. The one thing to fix is entry [11]: "gaano karaming paggamit ang nagastos" literally says the usage was "spent," which is an awkward way to render "incurred." Saying "gaano karami ang nagamit" would read more naturally.

examples.source: To determine how much usage a specific workload incurred
examples.translation: Para malaman kung gaano karaming paggamit ang nagastos ng isang partikular na workload
examples.suggested: Para malaman kung gaano karami ang nagamit ng isang partikular na workload
examples.why: This literally says the usage was 'spent' (nagastos), which is a calque of 'incurred'. Pairing paggamit with nagastos sounds stiff; the verb nagamit alone says it naturally.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The caveat that measuring only some systems affects the unmeasured ones is kept, and the terms quantum state, measurement and entanglement are consistent, with correlations rendered as "ugnayan". Several sentences copy English word order. "Isang simple ngunit kritikal na mahalagang ideya" and "napakadirektang humahantong" are literal calques. [6] opens with "May higit pa, gayunpaman, sa pag-unawa…", which is English syntax with "however" dropped into the middle of the clause, and a native technical writer would rephrase it. The informal register holds, with no po/opo.

examples.source: There is, however, more to understanding multiple quantum systems than simply recognizing that they may be viewed collectively as single systems.
examples.translation: May higit pa, gayunpaman, sa pag-unawa sa maraming quantum system kaysa simpleng pagkilala na maaari silang tingnan nang kolektibo bilang iisang sistema.
examples.suggested: Gayunpaman, hindi sapat na kilalanin lang na puwedeng tingnan nang sama-sama ang maraming quantum system bilang iisang sistema para lubos itong maunawaan.
examples.why: This copies the English 'There is, however, more to...' structure word for word, with the conjunction placed mid-clause, so it reads as translationese.

examples.source: A simple, yet critically important idea to keep in mind going into this lesson
examples.translation: Isang simple ngunit kritikal na mahalagang ideya na dapat tandaan sa pagtungo sa araling ito ay ... iisang, pinagsama-samang sistema
examples.suggested: Isang simple pero napakahalagang ideya na dapat tandaan sa pagsisimula ng araling ito ay ... iisang pinagsama-samang sistema
examples.why: 'Kritikal na mahalaga' and 'sa pagtungo sa' are literal calques, and the comma in 'iisang, pinagsama-samang' is carried over from English punctuation.

examples.source: this idea very directly leads to a description of how quantum states, measurements, and operations work
examples.translation: ang ideyang ito ay napakadirektang humahantong sa paglalarawan
examples.suggested: direktang humahantong ang ideyang ito sa paglalarawan
examples.why: 'Napakadirektang' is a stiff word-for-word rendering of 'very directly'. The 'ay' inversion also makes the sentence heavier than it needs to be.

editor_note: Entry [38] changes what the page teaches. "entirely analogous way" and "analogous properties" become "ganap na magkaparehong paraan" and "magkaparehong katangian", which say quantum measurement is completely identical to classical measurement rather than analogous to it. The same entry turns "trivial" into "walang kahulugan" (meaningless). Elsewhere, [63] turns "for the sake of tidiness" into "Para sa kadakilaan" ("for the sake of greatness"), and the coin flip / fan switch use "palipat/ipalipat/palipatin", which is the wrong verb (should be "ihagis" / "ilipat"). There are also smaller problems: [4] opens with a stray "Pala,", [54] has garbled calqued syntax, and "matrix" is inconsistent ("square matrix" and "stochastic matrix" alongside "matris" / "stochastic na matris").

examples.source: while quantum systems behave in an entirely analogous way ... By establishing the analogous properties of classical systems
examples.translation: habang ang mga quantum na sistema ay kumikilos sa isang ganap na magkaparehong paraan ... ng mga magkaparehong katangian
examples.suggested: habang kumikilos ang mga quantum na sistema sa lubos na kahalintulad na paraan ... ng mga kahalintulad na katangian
examples.why: 'Magkapareho' means identical, so the sentence now says quantum measurement behaves exactly like classical measurement. The source only says it is analogous, and a learner could come away with the false idea that the two are the same.

examples.source: This may seem trivial, and in some sense it is.
examples.translation: Maaaring mukhang walang kahulugan ito, at sa ilang paraan ay ganoon nga.
examples.suggested: Maaaring mukhang napakasimple o halata ito, at sa isang banda ay ganoon nga.
examples.why: 'Trivial' means obvious or simple, not meaningless. The translation says the point has no meaning, which undercuts the lesson.

examples.source: For the sake of tidiness, we write this product as
examples.translation: Para sa kadakilaan, isinusulat natin ang produktong ito bilang
examples.suggested: Para sa kaayusan/kalinisan ng notasyon, isinusulat natin ang produktong ito bilang
examples.why: 'Kadakilaan' means greatness or grandeur. It is the wrong word here and makes the sentence nonsensical.

examples.source: Suppose we flip a fair coin, but cover up the coin before looking at it.
examples.translation: Ipagpalagay na nagpalipat tayo ng isang patas na barya
examples.suggested: Ipagpalagay na naghagis tayo ng isang patas na barya
examples.why: 'Nagpalipat' means made something move or transfer. Coin tossing is 'maghagis/ihagis'. The same problem appears as 'ipalipat' in [39] and 'palipatin' in [13].

examples.source: makes use of an analogous notation for row vectors to the one for column vectors discussed previously
examples.translation: gumagamit ng katulad na notasyon para sa mga row vector sa isa para sa mga column vector na tinalakay noon
examples.suggested: gumagamit ng notasyon para sa mga row vector na kahalintulad ng notasyong tinalakay natin para sa mga column vector
examples.why: 'sa isa para sa' is a word-for-word calque of 'to the one for' and is hard to parse in Tagalog.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful and nothing here would mislead a learner, but there are a few small consistency and wording problems. 'Teams' is 'mga team' in [0] but 'koponan' in [5] and [11]. 'Quantum initiative' also shifts between an English kept term in [0] ('quantum initiative') and a translated one in [5] and [8] ('quantum na inisyatibo'). In [8], 'startup leadership' becomes the abstract noun 'pamumuno ng mga startup' in a list that otherwise names people ('mga lider', 'mga akademikong guro'), so the list no longer matches itself.

examples.source: A guide for teams and organizations in the early stages of quantum initiative development.
examples.translation: Isang gabay para sa mga team at organisasyon na nasa maagang yugto ng pagbuo ng quantum initiative.
examples.suggested: Isang gabay para sa mga koponan at organisasyon na nasa maagang yugto ng pagbuo ng mga quantum na inisyatibo.
examples.why: Entries [5] and [11] use 'koponan' for teams and [5] and [8] use 'quantum na inisyatibo'. This entry leaves both in English, so the page is inconsistent.

examples.source: including academic faculty, project leaders in large enterprises, startup leadership, and more
examples.translation: kabilang ang mga akademikong guro, mga lider ng proyekto sa malalaking negosyo, pamumuno ng mga startup, at iba pa
examples.suggested: kabilang ang mga akademikong guro, mga lider ng proyekto sa malalaking negosyo, mga namumuno sa mga startup, at iba pa
examples.why: 'Pamumuno' is the abstract act of leading, but every other item in this list is a group of people. A reader would expect the leaders themselves here.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner: the "not known, and possibly don't exist" caveat, the fragility and isolation tension, and the Shor code and discretization of errors framing all survive. In entry [3], "efficient" appears twice with its complexity-theory meaning but is translated two ways, first as "mahusay" (good/excellent) and then as "epektibong". "Mahusay" loses the technical sense. In entry [4], "some viewed that" becomes "may ilang nakakita na" ("some saw that"), which is a stiff calque; "may ilang naniniwala na" would sound more natural.

examples.source: to enable efficient solutions to computational tasks for which efficient classical algorithms are not known
examples.translation: magbigay ng mahusay na solusyon sa mga computational na gawain na wala pang kilalang epektibong klasikal na algorithm
examples.suggested: magbigay ng episyenteng solusyon ... na wala pang kilalang episyenteng klasikal na algorithm
examples.why: 'Efficient' is a technical term from complexity theory and is used twice in parallel here. Rendering it as 'mahusay' (good) and then 'epektibong' breaks the parallel and blurs the technical meaning.

examples.source: some viewed that the fragility of quantum information ... would ultimately make quantum computing impossible
examples.translation: may ilang nakakita na ang karupukan ng quantum information ... ay sa huli ay gagawing imposible ang quantum computing
examples.suggested: may ilang naniniwala na ang karupukan ng quantum information ... ang sa huli ay magpapaimposible sa quantum computing
examples.why: 'Nakakita' (saw) is a literal calque of 'viewed'. 'Naniniwala' or 'nag-akala' is how a native writer would express the opinion, and the doubled 'ay ... ay' is clunky.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The threshold-theorem caveats in [5] and [7] survive intact: below a finite threshold, and *hindi* nakasalalay sa laki ng circuit. A few spots read as calques. In [5], "kritikal na mahalagang katotohanan" copies "critically important" word for word. In [4], "maaaring matamaan ng mga error" has no subject, and "hindi natin maaaring i-decode" drops the "can't risk" nuance. The casual register holds and terms stay consistent (qubit, gate, measurement, logical qubit, threshold value).

examples.source: We'll discuss this critically important fact
examples.translation: Tatalakayin natin ang kritikal na mahalagang katotohanang ito
examples.suggested: Tatalakayin natin ang napakahalagang katotohanang ito
examples.why: 'kritikal na mahalaga' copies the English adverb+adjective pattern word for word; 'napakahalaga' or 'lubhang mahalaga' is what a native writer would use.

examples.source: we certainly can't risk decoding qubits ... because errors might strike when the protection ... is absent
examples.translation: hindi natin maaaring i-decode ang mga qubit ... dahil maaaring matamaan ng mga error habang wala ang proteksyon
examples.suggested: hindi natin kayang isugal na i-decode ang mga qubit ... dahil maaaring tamaan ng mga error ang mga qubit habang wala ang proteksyon
examples.why: 'matamaan ng mga error' has no subject, so it is unclear what gets hit. The translation also drops the 'risk' framing and turns it into a plain prohibition.

examples.source: which can detect and allow for the correction of errors
examples.translation: na kayang mag-detect at magpahintulot sa pagwawasto ng mga error
examples.suggested: na kayang mag-detect ng mga error at gawing posible ang pagwawasto sa mga ito
examples.why: 'magpahintulot sa pagwawasto' is a stiff calque of 'allow for'. It reads like permission rather than enablement.

editor_note: The page is faithful and reads naturally. Entry [3] has two small problems that don't mislead. The relative clause "mga code na kaya nilang tiisin ang mas mataas na error rate" is garbled: "nilang" adds a stray agent, as if other codes do the tolerating, so a native editor would write "mga code na kayang tumiis ng...". It also drops the intensifier "much" ("much higher" became just "mas mataas"), which weakens the lesson's contrast with the low-tolerance Shor, Steane and 5-qubit codes. Entries [2], [4], [5] and [6] are accurate: "error rate", "toric code" and "surface codes" are kept consistently, and the "positive integer greater than one" condition is kept exactly.

examples.source: including codes that can tolerate a much higher error rate than the ones we've seen so far
examples.translation: kabilang ang mga code na kaya nilang tiisin ang mas mataas na error rate kaysa sa mga nakita natin noon
examples.suggested: kabilang ang mga code na kayang tumiis ng mas mataas na mataas na error rate... → kabilang ang mga code na kayang tumiis ng mas mataas pang error rate kaysa sa mga nakita natin sa ngayon
examples.why: "na kaya nilang tiisin ... ang" is a broken relative clause with a stray agent pronoun. The codes themselves should be the ones doing the tolerating.

examples.source: a much higher error rate
examples.translation: mas mataas na error rate
examples.suggested: mas mataas nang husto na error rate / di-hamak na mas mataas na error rate
examples.why: The intensifier "much" was dropped. That weakens the contrast with the low-tolerance codes from earlier lessons, but it doesn't teach anything false.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The worst-case O(√N) optimality claim, the lower bound that was known before Grover's algorithm and the amplitude-amplification caveat "quadratically faster than classically" are all intact. A few phrases read as calques. "pundamental na mahalagang quantum algorithm" [6] stacks two adjectives stiffly. "itinugma ... ang isang lower bound" [3] is a literal rendering of "matched"; "tinapatan" would read better. "nang partikular" [2] is a word-for-word copy of "specifically".

examples.source: it is a fundamentally important quantum algorithm
examples.translation: ito ay isang pundamental na mahalagang quantum algorithm
examples.suggested: ito ay isang napakahalaga at pundamental na quantum algorithm
examples.why: Stacking 'pundamental na mahalagang' is a stiff calque of the English adverb+adjective.

examples.source: Grover's algorithm matched an already-known lower bound
examples.translation: itinugma ng Grover's algorithm ang isang lower bound na kilala na noon
examples.suggested: tinapatan ng Grover's algorithm ang isang lower bound na kilala na noon
examples.why: 'itinugma' means actively pairing or matching things up. 'tinapatan' (met or equalled) says more naturally that the algorithm reaches the bound.

examples.source: or even the *Unique search* problem specifically
examples.translation: o kahit ang problemang *Unique search* nang partikular
examples.suggested: o kahit ang mismong problemang *Unique search*
examples.why: 'nang partikular' is a word-for-word copy of 'specifically'. 'mismo' is the natural Tagalog way to give this emphasis.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: the quadratic and square-root cost claim in [3], the caveat about practical advantage in [5] and the quicksort/merge sort comparison in [6] all come through correctly. A few small edits remain. In [5], "much more advanced" loses its intensifier and becomes just "mas advanced", and "mukhang hindi malamang" is a stiff double hedge. In [9], "Finally" is rendered "Sa wakas", which reads as "at long last" rather than marking the last item in a sequence ("Panghuli"). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Classical computing hardware is much more advanced than quantum computing hardware
examples.translation: Ang klasikal na computing hardware ay mas advanced kaysa sa quantum computing hardware
examples.suggested: Ang klasikal na computing hardware ay mas higit na advanced kaysa sa quantum computing hardware
examples.why: The intensifier 'much' is dropped, which softens the gap the lesson stresses. Minor, since the direction of the comparison is kept.

examples.source: seems unlikely to lead to a practical advantage
examples.translation: mukhang hindi malamang na makapagbibigay ng praktikal na kalamangan
examples.suggested: malamang na hindi magbibigay ng praktikal na kalamangan
examples.why: 'mukhang hindi malamang' stacks two hedges and reads as a calque of 'seems unlikely'.

examples.source: Finally, he addresses the optimization of this algorithm
examples.translation: Sa wakas, tinugunan niya ang optimization ng algorithm na ito
examples.suggested: Panghuli, tinalakay niya ang optimization ng algorithm na ito
examples.why: 'Sa wakas' means 'at long last'. 'Panghuli' is the natural word for the last item in a list.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally in casual Tagalog: "algorithm ni Shor", "quantum Fourier transform" and "phase estimation" are kept consistently, and "ipatupad nang episyente ng isang quantum circuit" keeps the efficiency claim intact.

The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The caveats about replacing classical computers ("kung mangyari man") and the focus on scaling come through intact. A native editor would still fix a few calques. In [3], "given explicitly" became "ibinibigay nang malinaw", which means "given clearly", when the English means tahasan/direkta. In [6], "lalapit tayo sa" is an odd rendering of "turn to", and "kritikal na mahalaga" and "Partikular na," are word-for-word calques. In [5], "upang kilalanin ang katotohanan" reads as "in order to recognize" rather than "in recognition of". In [8], "pundasyon ng quantum algorithmic" leaves the English adjective without a noun.

examples.source: where problem inputs are given explicitly rather than in the form of an oracle
examples.translation: ibinibigay nang malinaw imbes na sa anyo ng isang oracle
examples.suggested: ibinibigay nang tahasan (direkta) imbes na sa anyo ng isang oracle
examples.why: 'malinaw' means 'clearly', not 'explicitly'. The contrast being drawn is that the input is given directly rather than hidden behind a black box.

examples.source: Finally, we'll turn to a critically important task ... Specifically, classical computations...
examples.translation: Sa wakas, lalapit tayo sa isang kritikal na mahalagang gawain ... Partikular na, ang mga klasikal na computation...
examples.suggested: Sa huli, babalingan natin ang isang napakahalagang gawain ... Sa partikular, ang mga klasikal na computation...
examples.why: These are calqued phrasings. 'lalapit tayo sa' does not mean 'turn to (a topic)', and 'kritikal na mahalaga' is a word-for-word copy of the English.

examples.source: We focus on this aspect of computational cost in recognition of the fact that algorithms have fundamental importance
examples.translation: Ito ang ating pinagtutuunan ng pansin upang kilalanin ang katotohanan na ang mga algorithm ay may pundamental na kahalagahan
examples.suggested: Ito ang pinagtutuunan natin dahil kinikilala nating may pundamental na kahalagahan ang mga algorithm
examples.why: 'upang kilalanin' turns the reason into a purpose ('in order to recognize'), and the phrasing is stiff.

examples.source: this lesson on quantum algorithmic foundations
examples.translation: araling ito tungkol sa mga pundasyon ng quantum algorithmic
examples.suggested: araling ito tungkol sa mga pundasyon ng mga quantum algorithm
examples.why: The English adjective 'algorithmic' is left without a noun, so the phrase is ungrammatical in Tagalog.

editor_note: The meaning is accurate throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The query-model caveat ("matigas at hindi natural sa diwang hindi nito tumpak na kinakatawan...") is kept, and so is the claim that Simon's algorithm gives a stronger advantage. In [4], "power" is calqued as "nagpapalakas" ("strengthen/boost"), which suggests the techniques make Shor's algorithm stronger rather than underlie it; "pinagbabatayan ng" or "nagpapatakbo sa" would read more naturally. Also in [4], "nagkataong isang napaka-kapaki-pakinabang na framework din" copies English "happens to be" word for word and reads stiffly.

examples.line_approx: Kabilang dito ang mga nagpapalakas sa pinakasikat na mga quantum algorithm
examples.source: This includes the ones that power the most well-known quantum algorithms
examples.translation: Kabilang dito ang mga nagpapalakas sa pinakasikat na mga quantum algorithm
examples.suggested: Kabilang dito ang mga teknik na pinagbabatayan ng pinakasikat na mga quantum algorithm
examples.why: 'nagpapalakas' means strengthen/boost, a literal calque of 'power'. The intended sense is that the techniques underlie these algorithms.

examples.line_approx: Ang query model ay nagkataong isang napaka-kapaki-pakinabang na framework din
examples.source: The query model also happens to be a very useful framework for explaining
examples.translation: Ang query model ay nagkataong isang napaka-kapaki-pakinabang na framework din para sa *pagpapaliwanag*
examples.suggested: Napaka-kapaki-pakinabang din ang query model bilang framework sa *pagpapaliwanag*
examples.why: 'nagkataong' copies English 'happens to be' word for word and sounds stiff in Tagalog.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. Discrimination (identify which state from a known set was prepared) and tomography (rebuild a density matrix from many copies of an unknown state) are both rendered faithfully. The one thing I would change is the word for "measurement". The file uses the bare noun "sukat", which usually means size or dimension. That makes phrases like "nagsagawa ng sukat" and "susuriin natin ang mga sukat" read stiffly. A native editor would use the action noun "pagsukat" / "mga pagsukat" for the act of measuring, and keep the English "measurement" where it is part of a term (projective measurements).

examples.source: When a measurement is performed on a system in a quantum state
examples.translation: Kapag nagsagawa ng sukat sa isang sistema na nasa quantum state
examples.suggested: Kapag nagsagawa ng pagsukat sa isang sistemang nasa quantum state
examples.why: Here 'sukat' reads as size or dimension. The act of measuring is 'pagsukat', which also reads more naturally with 'nagsagawa'.

examples.source: In this lesson we'll consider measurements in greater generality.
examples.translation: Sa araling ito, susuriin natin ang mga sukat sa mas pangkalahatang paraan.
examples.suggested: Sa araling ito, susuriin natin ang mga pagsukat sa mas pangkalahatang paraan.
examples.why: Same problem: 'mga sukat' can be read as 'dimensions'. Using 'pagsukat' consistently would make the lesson's core concept clear.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The purification definition, the "provided that the traced-out portion is large enough" caveat, and the fidelity/Uhlmann's theorem framing all come through intact. There are two small slips. In [4], "restricting" in the dilation sentence becomes "paghihigpit", which reads as "tightening/making strict" rather than the mathematical sense of restricting to a subsystem. In [3], "fundamentally important concept" is shortened to "pundamental na konsepto", which drops the emphasis on importance.

examples.source: where something relatively complicated is obtained by restricting or reducing something larger yet simpler
examples.translation: sa pamamagitan ng paghihigpit o pagbabawas ng isang mas malaki ngunit mas simpleng bagay
examples.suggested: sa pamamagitan ng pag-restrict o pag-reduce sa isang mas malaki ngunit mas simpleng bagay
examples.why: In this context 'restricting' is a mathematical operation (restricting to a part of a system). 'Paghihigpit' means tightening or making stricter, so it hides that sense.

examples.source: a fundamentally important concept in the theory of quantum information
examples.translation: isang pundamental na konsepto sa teorya ng quantum information
examples.suggested: isang napakahalaga at pundamental na konsepto sa teorya ng quantum information
examples.why: 'Important' is dropped, which weakens the emphasis the English puts on how central purification is.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. That includes the information-theory origin of "channel", "ingay" for noise, and the equivalence of the three representations. There are three small slips. In the video title (entry 8), "reviews various representations" became "Binibigyang-kahulugan niya" ("he defines/interprets"); "Sinusuri" or "Nirerepaso" would be accurate. In entry 5, the adjective is "matematikong termino" in one sentence and "matematikang paglalarawan" in the next. Also in entry 5, "isang maliit na seleksyon ng mga halimbawa" is a stiff calque of "small selection of examples".

examples.source: He reviews various representations of quantum channels
examples.translation: Binibigyang-kahulugan niya ang iba't ibang representasyon ng mga quantum channel
examples.suggested: Sinusuri niya ang iba't ibang representasyon ng mga quantum channel
examples.why: 'Binibigyang-kahulugan' means 'defines/interprets', not 'reviews'. It is a small change in meaning, but it does not mislead.

examples.source: in mathematical terms ... equivalent mathematical characterizations
examples.translation: sa mga matematikong termino ... magkakatumbas na matematikang paglalarawan
examples.suggested: sa matematikal na paraan ... magkakatumbas na matematikal na paglalarawan
examples.why: The adjective for 'mathematical' is spelled two different ways in consecutive sentences.

examples.source: along with a small selection of examples
examples.translation: kasama ang isang maliit na seleksyon ng mga halimbawa
examples.suggested: kasama ang ilang halimbawa
examples.why: This is a literal calque. A native technical writer would just say 'ilang halimbawa'.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and natural throughout: the optional-content caveat in [6] ("maliban sa mga may markang opsyonal"), the 2–3 hour estimate in [7] and the conditional badging exam in [9] ("kung nais mo") all carry over intact, and "resources" is rendered consistently as "mapagkukunan" in a casual register with no po/opo.

All three entries are faithful and read naturally in casual Tagalog: "Ituloy ang iyong paglalakbay sa pag-aaral", "Paparating na ang aralin!", and the untranslated product name "IBM Quantum Platform".

Nothing here would mislead a learner, but a native editor would change two phrasings. Entry [0] keeps the English compound "14-lesson course" and "learning asset". Entry [4] correctly uses "14 na aralin", so the page treats the same idea two ways. Also in [4], "halos katulad na katulad" is a redundant, stiff rendering of "very similar". It stacks "halos" (almost) on the intensifying reduplication, and "halos kapareho" or "katulad na katulad" alone would read more naturally.

examples.source: A collection of learning assets from a 14-lesson course on utility-scale quantum computing.
examples.translation: Isang koleksyon ng mga learning asset mula sa 14-lesson course tungkol sa utility-scale quantum computing.
examples.suggested: Isang koleksyon ng mga materyales sa pag-aaral mula sa isang kursong may 14 na aralin tungkol sa utility-scale quantum computing.
examples.why: Keeps the English compound "14-lesson course", while [4] renders the same idea as "14 na aralin". This is a calque and is inconsistent within the page.

examples.source: The result is very similar to work published on the cover of Nature in June 2023.
examples.translation: Ang resulta ay halos katulad na katulad ng gawaing nailathala sa cover ng Nature noong Hunyo 2023.
examples.suggested: Ang resulta ay halos kapareho ng gawaing nailathala sa cover ng Nature noong Hunyo 2023.
examples.why: "halos" + "katulad na katulad" is a redundant, awkward stack of hedge and intensifier. A native writer would pick one of them.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning holds throughout, including the lesson ranges, the note that there is no quiz or badge, and the deprecation caveat. A few spots read like translation artifacts. Entry [3] leaves an editor's slash option in the text ("payak/kakaunti ang laman"). Entry [8] adds a redundant gloss in parentheses ("nang may mabuting loob (matapat na pagtatantya)"). Entry [5] uses the stiff calque "naka-host nang panlabas". In entry [4], "tangential ... to which we are building" became "pangalawa lamang ... na ating binubuo", which shifts the meaning slightly to "secondary to the calculation we are building" when the source means "peripheral to the calculation we are working toward".

examples.source: the labs are sparse and merely show a workflow
examples.translation: ang mga lab ay payak/kakaunti ang laman at nagpapakita lamang ng isang workflow
examples.suggested: ang mga lab ay maikli lang at nagpapakita lamang ng isang workflow
examples.why: The slash alternative is an unresolved translator choice. Published prose would never contain it.

examples.source: Good-faith estimates of required QPU time have been provided at the top of each lesson
examples.translation: Ang mga pagtatantya ng kinakailangang oras ng QPU ay ginawa nang may mabuting loob (matapat na pagtatantya) at ibinigay sa tuktok ng bawat aralin
examples.suggested: May matapat na tantiya ng kinakailangang oras ng QPU sa itaas ng bawat aralin
examples.why: The gloss in parentheses repeats the idea and makes the sentence heavy and robotic.

examples.source: and is hosted externally on GitHub
examples.translation: at naka-host nang panlabas sa GitHub
examples.suggested: at nasa labas ng site na ito, sa GitHub
examples.why: 'Naka-host nang panlabas' is a literal calque of 'hosted externally'.

examples.source: they are mostly tangential to the utility-scale calculation to which we are building
examples.translation: karamihan sa mga ito ay pangalawa lamang sa utility-scale na kalkulasyon na ating binubuo
examples.suggested: hindi sila gaanong direktang kaugnay ng utility-scale na kalkulasyong pinupuntahan natin
examples.why: 'Pangalawa lamang' means 'secondary', not 'peripheral'. 'Binubuo' drops the sense of 'building toward'. The shift is slight and does not mislead.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful in every entry. The Open Plan free-time caveat, the simulator fallback and the "2×2 matrices should be sufficient" note all come through, and the casual register holds with no po/opo. Two phrasings are stiff. In [5], "mas maikli nang husto na panahon" is an awkward calque of "much less time". In [4], "eksperimentong tuklasin" uses the adjective form where an adverb is needed ("tuklasin nang eksperimental"). Neither would mislead a learner.

examples.source: All activities can be completed in much less time than the free time allotted
examples.translation: maaaring makumpleto sa mas maikli nang husto na panahon kaysa sa libreng oras na inilaan
examples.suggested: maaaring matapos sa mas maikling oras, malayo pa sa libreng oras na inilaan
examples.why: 'mas maikli nang husto na panahon' is a clumsy calque of 'much less time' that a native writer wouldn't use. The meaning is intact.

examples.source: to experimentally explore foundational quantum protocols
examples.translation: upang eksperimentong tuklasin ang mga pangunahing quantum protocol
examples.suggested: upang tuklasin nang eksperimental ang mga pangunahing quantum protocol
examples.why: 'eksperimentong' is the adjective form used where an adverb is needed. It reads stiffly.

editor_note: The three entries are faithful: the heading "Modules" is rendered as "Mga Module", and the link labels "Computer Science" and "Quantum Mechanics" stay in English, which is a defensible choice for module titles.

The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. In [4], "matatapos nang mas maikli pa nang malayo kaysa sa libreng oras" is an awkward calque of "much less than the free time"; a native editor would write something like "matatapos sa mas maikling oras kaysa". Entry [9] adds "(walang kailangang baguhin)", which is not in the English. It is harmless because it only clarifies "run as written". Terms are handled consistently: module, superposition, and simulator stay in English, and uncertainty is rendered as "kawalan ng katiyakan".

examples.source: All activities can be completed in much less than the free time allotted as part of the Open Plan
examples.translation: Lahat ng aktibidad ay matatapos nang mas maikli pa nang malayo kaysa sa libreng oras na inilaan
examples.suggested: Lahat ng aktibidad ay matatapos sa mas maikling oras kaysa sa libreng oras na inilaan
examples.why: "mas maikli pa nang malayo" is a stiff word-for-word rendering of "much less than" and reads as machine translation.

examples.source: though most notebooks can simply be run as written
examples.translation: bagaman karamihan sa mga notebook ay puwedeng patakbuhin gaya ng pagkakasulat (walang kailangang baguhin)
examples.suggested: bagaman karamihan sa mga notebook ay puwedeng patakbuhin na lang gaya ng pagkakasulat
examples.why: The parenthetical is not in the source. It does not mislead, but the word "simply" is dropped and replaced by an explanation the translator added.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. The table descriptions are accurate, for example "Bawasan ang circuit width at depth sa pamamagitan ng pagputol ng mga gate at wire" and "pagtatantiya ng ground state", and field terms like error mitigation, circuit depth and tensor network are kept in English consistently.
